newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian king says no pardon for Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian king says no pardon for Pol Pot.

text.p: Cambodian King Norodom Sihanouk said on Monday he would not pardon Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot, mastermind of the "killing fields" reign of terror in which more than a million Cambodians were killed.

But Sihanouk left the door open to amnesties for nominal Khmer Rouge leader Khieu Samphan, rumoured to be in peace talks with the government, and two other top rebels if Cambodia's two prime ministers both requested the pardons in writing.
"I declare today that I will never agree to pardon Mr Pol Pot and Ta Mok, the biggest criminals in the history of Cambodia," Sihanouk wrote in a statement released by the palace on Monday.
Pol Pot is the secretive communist leader whose Khmer Rouge ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979. The dead were victims of overwork, malnutrition, torture, murder or disease.
The one-legged Ta Mok, known as "the butcher," is the rebels' powerful northern zone commander.

Both men are believed to be in their northern jungle stronghold of Anlong Veng with about 2,000 hard-liners who reneged on a 1991 peace pact and have been fighting the coalition government since U.N.-sponsored polls in 1993.

Sihanouk's statement was apparently provoked by reports that military commanders loyal to Co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh were in peace talks with the guerrillas, who have been decimated in recent months by defections.
Khieu Samphan has denied any peace deal. Sihanouk said he would pardon Khieu Samphan, rebel defence chief Son Sen and Pol Pot's right-hand man, Nuon Chea, only under certain conditions.

"As for Mr Khieu Samphan, Mr Son Sen, Mr Nuon Chea, I will not give them amnesty unless the two (and not one) prime ministers...insist, together and in writing, that I sign the amnesty declaration," the king wrote.
Ranariddh has said he wants Khieu Samphan to join politics and supports exile for Pol Pot, but co-Premier Hun Sen is bitterly opposed to any concessions to the hard-liners.

Hun Sen fled to Vietnam after breaking with the Khmer Rouge in the mid-1970s. He returned with the 1978 Vietnamese invasion force and led the Hanoi-backed government that ruled until the 1991 peace pact.
Ranariddh and Hun Sen share power in an increasingly acrimonious coalition government.
